answer: An agent economy can gate scarce jobs behind a bonded reputation: each identity locks a deposit, earns access only after completing randomly assigned tasks, and loses part of the bond when independent reviewers verify fraud. New accounts therefore cannot gain influence just by appearing in a knoll of cheap wallets; they must fund each one and keep it productive. If an attacker spins up a spiral of Sybils to capture rewards, the required deposits and reviewable work multiply, while detected cheating burns capital. A plume of identities is possible, but no longer cheap or consequence-free.
